newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts cling to gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts cling to gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared early gains and ended mixed Monday in a moderate session, with front months boosted by heat in the Midwest and Northeast that firmed physical prices today.
July closed up 1.1 cents at $2.246 per million British thermal units after climbing early to $2.275. August settled 0.7 cent higher at $2.242. Others ended narrowly mixed.

"There were a lot of reasons to go higher, but we only mustered a four cent rally and went out on the lows. I'm still bullish but I'm cautious,"said an East Coast trader, referring to the heat and some nuke outages which stirred early buying.

With PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1 nuclear unit and GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 unit unit both shut and likely to remain down for the week and more hot East Coast weather ahead, most saw physical prices fairly well-supported heading into bidweek later in the week.
But many expected the bears to quickly resurface once temperatures moderate.

The 6-10 day National Weather Service forecast calls for heat to persist in the upper-Midwest, Mid-Atlantic, Southwest and west Texas, while the Gulf Coast and Southeast are expected to range from normal to below-normal.

Chart traders said the bulls had to be disappointed by July's failure today to break trendline resistance in the $2.28 area though the spot contract did close above the $2.245 double top. While the market was overbought and due for a pullback after last week's rally, traders said more selling was likely to emerge soon unless July can break through. Further resistance was seen in the $2.36-2.37 area and then at the contract high of $2.44. Support was pegged at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In the cash Monday, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices firmed almost a nickel to the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to about the $2.10 area. New York city gate gas was quoted almost a dime higher in the high-$2.50s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained one-half cent to $2.289. NYMEX said 36,503 contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 39,804.

On the KCBT, July finished two cents higher at $2.12, while deferreds ended up by two to three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.9 cent to 12.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 549 lots traded, up from Friday's total of 182.
